article_notes: 102 dogs with babesiosis diagnosed by capillary blood smear (auricle) at a private clinic in Kharkiv, Ukraine, 2019; species not identified (probably B. canis). Text is an LLM translation from Ukrainian, not reviewed. Table 1 groups dogs by intensity of invasion (high n=29, medium n=38, low n=35) and gives counts/% with haemoglobinuria, icterus, raised body temperature and other signs; no statistical test. Rows record high (severe) vs low (comparison); medium group values in each note. The low group's 'affected erythrocytes' value (3,54±0,20, '1–5 in a smear') is higher than the medium group's and appears to be per smear rather than per field, so the grouping is as the authors assigned it. 'Others' = weakness, refusal of food, laboured breathing, dyspnoea, thirst. Table 2 (infected n=25 vs healthy n=10, 15 parameters) was not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: high vs medium vs low intensity of invasion
severity_definitions.definition: Intensity of invasion graded from capillary smears by affected erythrocytes per microscope field and parasites per erythrocyte: high (5,38±0,12 per field, 3-5 per RBC), medium (1,89±0,05, 1-3), low (1-5 per smear, 1-2). Rows compare high (severe) with low.
severity_definitions.comparison_group: low intensity of invasion (n=35); medium n=38
severity_definitions.quote: We studied the features of the clinical manifestation of the disease depending on the intensity of invasion (II) (Table 1).
